metadata.title: Matt Dillahunty vs Lewis Howitt: Is Christianity True?
metadata.label: Logic, reason, and divine grounding
metadata.motion: Is Christianity true, and do the grounding of logic, a necessary cause, divine hiddenness, and the relation of reason to revelation support or undermine it?
metadata.sourceNote: Assessment based exclusively on the complete locally cached YouTube caption transcript and timestamped events (transcript SHA-256 b764ef00b320fcfb77f79008de9cd0d0b74015a973628e9576f9b253740810d7). Required below-high-confidence audio checks were completed before adjudication; representative quotations must be exact strings from quote-eligible locked source spans.
metadata.scoringNote: Scores are AI-generated estimates of argumentative performance under the locked adjudicated-consensus workflow. Repository code calculated every move, section, and overall result once, only after two isolated judgments, required audio review, and disputed-field adjudication closed.

routes.description: Establish Christianity through a cumulative metaphysical route from unavoidable logic and contingent reality to a necessary self-relating Logos, then identify its universal, particular, and individual structure with the Trinity and defend the coherence of divine self-knowledge, creation, and hiddenness.
routes.successCriteria: The route succeeds if indispensable logical and explanatory relations require a necessary mental ground, the proposed structure warrants a specifically Trinitarian identification rather than generic theism, and the account remains coherent under objections concerning divine perfection, revelation, creation, and hiddenness.

motionBridge.description: Connect the necessary self-relating Logos to distinctively Christian Trinitarian truth rather than stopping at logic, a first cause, idealism, or generic divinity.

centralBridges.description: Show that logic is unavoidable and describes the objective self-relating structure of reality requiring the proposed Logos account.
Show that contingent reality and rational explanation terminate in an uncaused necessary foundation rather than an infinite regress or brute physical fact.
Justify identifying the interdependence of universality, particularity, and individuality with a mental and specifically Trinitarian Logos.
Reconcile divine perfection and timeless knowledge with self-relation, doubt, creation, and contingent truths without introducing contradiction or dependence.

subsidiaryBridges.description: Explain how natural reason can disclose the relevant Trinitarian structure while accounting for Christianity's historical and incarnational claims.
Show why religious doubt, historical variation, divine transcendence, and creation from nothing remain compatible with the proposed God.

routes.description: Reject the motion by applying correspondence, demonstration, and explanatory economy to the Logos case, showing that its inferences do not establish a unique necessary mind or Christianity and that hiddenness and internal tensions provide contrary evidence.
routes.successCriteria: The route succeeds if logic and reality can be treated without adding God, the transitions from first cause or logical categories to a mind and Trinity remain unsupported, or the proposed Christian account conflicts with divine perfection, historical accessibility, classical logic, or expected evidence.

motionBridge.description: Connect the affirmative case's evidential, inferential, or coherence failures to withholding affirmation that Christianity is true and to any supported contrary inference.

centralBridges.description: Defend correspondence with demonstrable reality and minimal explanatory commitments as the appropriate standard for the Christian truth claim.
Show that a regress terminus, necessary foundation, logical structure, or mind does not establish a unique cause, Trinity, incarnation, or Catholic Christianity.
Show that an omniscient perfect mind cannot genuinely doubt, learn, deliberate, or correct itself in the manner required by the affirmative account.
Defend content-neutral classical logical laws against the dialectical unity of opposites used to support the affirmative metaphysics.

subsidiaryBridges.description: Explain why divine hiddenness, unanswered prayer, religious competition, and historical variation count against the expected Christian world.
Distinguish conclusions arguably available through natural reason from historical claims about Jesus that require otherwise unavailable testimony or revelation.

sections.title: Truth Standards, Evidence, and Divine Hiddenness
sections.rationale: The motion requires a standard for affirming religious truth and an account of whether divine silence, disagreement, prayer, and historical variation fit or undermine Christianity.

sections.title: Grounding Logic and the Logos
sections.rationale: The central affirmative framework treats logic as unavoidable and as reality's objective self-relating structure, while the skeptical alternative disputes that God adds necessary grounding or explanation.

sections.title: Necessary Cause, Contingency, and Explanatory Termination
sections.rationale: The route from contingent reality to an uncaused foundation must establish an adequate terminus and address whether uniqueness, mentality, and explanatory resources follow from causal termination.

sections.title: From Metaphysical Structure to Trinity, Incarnation, and Revelation
sections.rationale: Christianity requires bridging generic metaphysical conclusions to the Trinity and historically specific claims about Jesus while resolving what natural reason can establish without revelation or testimony.

sections.title: Perfect Divine Knowledge, Doubt, and Self-Relation
sections.rationale: The extended dispute over whether perfect knowledge can include falsification, doubt, recursive correction, or foreknown resolution directly tests the coherence of the proposed Trinitarian mind and incarnation.

sections.title: Creation, Divine Relations, Spacetime, and Logical Coherence
sections.rationale: Claims about timeless creation, contingent truths, transcendence, spacetime, and unity of opposites test whether the proposed God can relate to creation without dependence, change, or conflict with classical logic.
